title: Rome: even before grace man has free choice in spiritual things, since aided he can embrace or reject the good
source_text: II. Primo enim Scholae Romanae Theologi, quantumlibet gratiae divinae auxilium ad pietatis opera necessarium agnoscant, nihilominus dici volunt hominem in rebus divinis & spiritualibus, etiam ante gratiam, esse Liberi arbitrii. Non quod in eo genere sine gratia quicquam possit, sed quia, mediante auxilio gratiae, libere potest bonum spirituale amplecti, & sic ut veram potestatem habeat illud rejiciendi, atque ab eo recedendi.
pass_a_gloss: II. For first the Theologians of the Roman School, however much they acknowledge the help of divine grace to be necessary for the works of piety, nevertheless will that man be said to be of free choice in divine and spiritual things, even before grace. Not that in that kind he can do anything without grace, but because, the help of grace mediating, he can freely embrace spiritual good, and so that he has a true power of rejecting it, and of departing from it.
pass_b_english: First, the theologians of the Roman School, however much they acknowledge that the help of divine grace is necessary for works of piety, still want it said that man has free choice in divine and spiritual things even before grace.

They do not mean that he can do anything of that kind without grace, but that, with the help of grace, he can freely embrace spiritual good, and in such a way that he has a real power to reject it and turn away from it.

lemmas.latin: etiam ante gratiam, esse Liberi arbitrii
lemmas.gloss: even before grace, to be of free choice
he has a true power of rejecting it

choices.why: The faculty of free decision; 'free choice' throughout, with 'freedom' for libertas.
